I farm only 5 mu, and I am 78, so I will keep things simple, steady, and low-risk. I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation because I know it well, it fits my land, and I have well irrigation, which gives me some security in dry periods. I will not chase complicated changes. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, put most fertilizer in at the base with a moderate topdressing, irrigate at the key stages, and keep field work simple with rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small area. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable yield, give it a bit more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when summer rain is not enough, and control weeds and insects with a limited number of pesticide sprays. Since some family members work off-farm, I will choose a plan that is manageable with limited labor and aims for reliable output instead of maximum output.
